facts.statement: The genus Palaeospheniscus was described by Moreno and Mercerat in 1891.
Palaeospheniscus is an extinct genus of penguins that belongs to the subfamily Palaeospheniscinae.
facts.quote: Palaeospheniscus is an extinct genus of penguins belonging to the subfamily Palaeospheniscinae.

facts.statement: Species of Palaeospheniscus ranged from medium-sized to large penguins, with lengths estimated between 55 cm and 73 cm.
facts.quote: The species of Palaeospheniscus were medium-sized to largish penguins, ranging from P. gracilis with an estimated maximal length of 55 cm to P. wimani, which reached up to 73 cm.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Palaeospheniscus patagonicus, known as the Patagonian slender-footed penguin.
facts.quote: The type species of this genus is Palaeospheniscus patagonicus, the Patagonian slender-footed penguin.

facts.statement: Most specimens of Palaeospheniscus were found in the Santa Cruz and Chubut provinces of Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Most of the specimens were found in Santa Cruz and Chubut Provinces of Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils of Palaeospheniscus were recovered from the Patagonian Molasse Formation and date to the Early Miocene, Late Miocene, or possibly Early Pliocene.
facts.quote: The fossils were recovered from the Patagonian Molasse Formation, and are probably Early Miocene to Late Miocene or possibly Early Pliocene in age (Stucchi et al. 2003).

facts.statement: Specimens of this genus have been found in the Pliocene of South Africa, the Miocene to Pliocene of Chile, the Miocene of Argentina and South Africa, and the Oligocene to Miocene of Argentina and Peru.
facts.quote: Specimen belonging to this genus have been found in the Pliocene of South Africa, in Miocene to Pliocene of Chile, in Miocene of Argentina and South Africa and in Oligocene to Miocene of Argentina and Peru.

facts.statement: Palaeospheniscus is classified within the family Spheniscidae.
The genus Palaeospheniscus was coined by François Moreno and Alcide Mercerat in 1891 to designate a series of fossil specimens from Argentine Patagonia.
facts.quote: El género Palaeospheniscus fue acuñado por François Moreno y Alcide Mercerat en 1891 para designar una serie de especímenes fósiles procedentes de la Patagonia argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype of the type species Palaeospheniscus patagonicus is an isolated tarsometatarsus (MLP 20-34) deposited in the Museo de La Plata, Argentina, from the Gaiman Formation (Early Miocene).
facts.quote: La especie tipo del género corresponde a Palaeospheniscus patagonicus, cuyo holotipo consiste en un tarsometatarso aislado (MLP 20-34) que se encuentra depositado en el Museo de La Plata, Argentina y proceden de la Formación Gaiman (Mioceno temprano).

facts.statement: The Patagonian genera Paraspheniscus, Trelewdyptes, Chubutodyptes, and Perispheniscus have currently been included in one of the three species of Palaeospheniscus.
facts.quote: Igualmente, los géneros patagónicos Paraspheniscus, Trelewdyptes, Chubutodyptes y Perispheniscus han sido actualmente incluidos en alguna de estas tres especies.

facts.statement: The time range for Palaeospheniscus is from the Aquitanian to the Zanclean, approximately 23.04 to 3.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Zanclean (23.04 to 3.6 million years ago)
